doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Listening and Liebman's demands over thirty years
summary: Liebman and Woods heard every note; Liebman wanted bass to break things up and loved colors.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Come on, man, listen. Dave Liebman, I’ll listen to every note. Phil Woods listened to every note. I mean when you get that level player there wasn’t one breath of music that © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

they missed. They were in there. And then the next day in the bus you know, talking about remembering what was good and what wasn’t good. They just were constantly – I mean Lieb was that way definitely, constantly on it. Never gave it up. Sometimes, uh oh, what’s he going to say now. “Letter A on -- ” Mostly the chord player. Mostly the chord players got it, I didn’t get much, I was lucky you know, I did my job. You know he wanted me to break things up. He didn’t want me to stay constant, and he wanted the drummer to be very open to any kind of groove change or just something to make the music exciting, and then colors. He was big into colors so whatever effects a guitar or piano would use or chords to change colors you know, that was what the band was based on you know.
So it was a great experience. Yeah. Lucky to have been doing that for 30 odd years.
